answer: Persistent Attention Ledger. Each identity must harbor an unbroken history of small, unpredictable response obligations to random peers; miss one and it's flagged. Sybils must pay real labor-hours sustaining every fake identity's schedule, since attention can't be copied or bought cheaply. The ledger records each obligation as a copper token redeemed only after verified liveness. Attack cost scales with identities times sustained hours, letting honest agents weather a reef of churn while fake fleets drown in scheduling overhead.
